title: Five files, three gates
spec: G06 · plan gate, diff gate, and your own terminal
intro: Recipe tagging touches storage, the API, search and two test files. You do not write those five files — you approve them, one gate at a time, and one of the gates is where you catch a real bug.

provenance.source: the Recipe Box app ships only inside the module HTML, not as project files; the ticket, GEMINI.md rules and the ordering bug in the diff are taken from the module, terminal output is reconstructed

foot: Run it for real: the module's lab ships the full six-requirement ticket to paste into Agent mode.

steps.title: Clean tree first, then a ticket instead of a wish
narrative: Two commands before you start an agent, every time: git status to prove the tree is clean, and pytest tests/ -v to record what green looked like beforehand. Without the first, git diff afterwards mixes your work with the agent's. Without the second, you cannot tell a test the agent broke from one that was already broken.

Then give it outcomes and constraints, not implementation. Six numbered requirements, one deliberate demand — explain the tradeoff you chose in the plan — because a JSON column and a join table are both defensible and you want to see whether it reasoned or defaulted. End with Show me your plan before editing until that is a habit.
steps.youDo: git status && pytest tests/ -v, then paste the six-requirement tagging ticket into Agent mode.

steps.title: Gate 1 — the plan, where corrections are cheapest
narrative: The plan comes back with a join table, and with the justification you asked for: a tags table plus a recipe_tags link table, because GET /recipes?tag=vegan is a filter and filtering a JSON column means scanning every row.

It also plans to DROP TABLE recipes and recreate it. Your database has data in it. Say so, in one sentence, in plain language — this is the cheapest intervention in the whole session, because no code exists yet to unwind.
Toggle Before / After. The correction cost you a sentence. The same correction discovered after five files were written would have cost the generation, the review, the revert and the regeneration.
steps.youDo: Read the plan against four questions: right files only? schema choice justified? migration or drop? tests at the end?

steps.title: Gate 2 — reject a diff, revert to the checkpoint
narrative: The agent takes a checkpoint before editing and presents storage.py first. Read every hunk against three questions: is it correct, is it in scope, and is it rule-compliant against your GEMINI.md?

This one fails the first question. The comprehension lowercases every tag, and the validation that tags must be non-empty strings runs on the line after it. Feed it a tag of 42 and .strip() raises AttributeError before the validator ever sees it. Reject the hunk and say exactly that: validate first, then normalize.

Reverting to the checkpoint restores files. It does not undo the side effects of commands you approved — a package installed, a table created, a row deleted. That asymmetry is why the command gate deserves more scrutiny than the diff gate, even though the diff gate is where you spend more time.
steps.youDo: Reject the hunk with a specific reason: "validation runs after the lowercase comprehension — reorder it".
steps.claudeSays: It reverts to checkpoint cp-2, restores storage.py, and re-emits the hunk with the validation loop above the normalization.

steps.title: Gate 3 — green in your terminal, not in its transcript
narrative: Four more diffs, four more approvals, and the agent asks to run pytest. Allow it — but expect a wrinkle. Two older tests assert the exact shape of a recipe dict and now see a tags key. Updating a test because the contract intentionally grew is legitimate. Weakening a test so a bug passes is not, and only you can tell those apart.

Then verify independently. git diff --stat tells you the footprint: five files, and only the five the ticket named. pytest tests/ -v in your own terminal tells you the result, which is a different claim from the agent reporting that it ran.

Toggle Before / After to see the applied-versus-pending ledger close. The commit message says what happened: agent-assisted, human-reviewed — because you corrected the plan, rejected a diff, and ran the tests yourself.
steps.youDo: git diff --stat, then pytest tests/ -v in your own terminal — before you commit anything.
